responses.review_design:2:1: fixed: new section 4a. validate_submit_output requires SHA.match for the override, with the reviewer's message. The rev_parse/ancestry checks in done_record stay. fill_current_records (verbs.py:917) gets the same full-sha rule, plus a 'does not exist' refusal where rev_parse returns None. The card wording is now 'give {"commit": "<full 40-hex sha>"}; ref names such as HEAD and short shas are refused', and prompts/CLI_USAGE match it. Tests: HEAD, 'main', a goal branch name, a short sha and uppercase hex each get validation; 'a'*40 is accepted; an end-to-end submit of HEAD is refused and the work-branch full sha succeeds; the existing 'not in the work branch' and 'does not exist' refusals still fire; the edit-completion cases are covered. Minor note: section 2 now says record_stale == ["def"] is kept on purpose (the 'If it still holds, resubmit it' hint is safe only when def alone changed).

output.summary: Attempt 3 of the G1016 design. It fixes F2 (review_design:2:1). A checkpoint override must now be a full 40-hex sha: validate_submit_output (schemas.py:933) adds SHA.match with the message 'a checkpoint override is {"commit": "<40-hex sha>"}; omit the key to use the default'. done_record keeps its rev_parse existence check and ancestry check. The same rule applies to the {"commit"}-only completion in fill_current_records (verbs.py:917), which also now refuses a commit that does not exist instead of storing None. The card text, the implement/test_design prompts and CLI_USAGE now say ref names such as HEAD and short shas are refused. New tests: schema-level refusal of HEAD, branch names, a short sha and uppercase hex, with a full sha accepted; an end-to-end submit refusal for HEAD; and edit-time completion. The previous.output rule is settled on purpose as record_stale == ["def"], today's exact match, because its 'resubmit it' hint is safe only when the definition alone changed. Everything else is unchanged from attempt 2.

findings.text: Reclaim cards would wrongly downgrade capability. card.build sets cap='routine' when stale_because == ['inputs.base'] (card.py:79-80), a rule meant for record-stale rebases. The design puts lease-since-claim staleness on reclaim cards and says existing stale_because rules apply unchanged, so a reclaimed no-record implement or test_design (both consume inputs.base, and base re-runs whenever integration moves) gets capability 'routine' and is routed to the cheapest models for a full first run; same for a reclaimed reopened run. Fix: key the routine downgrade on staleness against a done record only (e.g. the record-stale set, not the union), or only when the abandoned lease's reason was 'stale'; add a test that a no-record implement reclaimed after base moved keeps its own capability. While editing output_schema, also consider: non-review finding_effect should say the phase re-runs 'if that ancestor's output changes' (a dispute leaves it current), and the artifact text should say --artifact takes the local file while artifact.path is where submit stores it.

Checkpoint overrides must be a full 40-hex sha. At 54d7e83, schemas.py:933 accepts {"commit": <any str>}, and done_record (verbs.py:459) resolves it with s.git.rev_parse, which runs in the main repository (gitrun.py:79, cwd=self.primary), not the goal worktree. {"commit": "HEAD"} therefore resolves to the main checkout's HEAD, usually an integration commit and so an ancestor of the work branch. It passes the is_ancestor check, and the base is recorded as the checkpoint silently. Ref names (main, dev, worktree-only branches) behave the same way. The design's new card text says the literal "HEAD" is refused, which is not true at read_dev. Fix: in validate_submit_output, require SHA.match for the override (message: a checkpoint override is {"commit": "<40-hex sha>"}; omit the key to use the default). Keep the rev_parse and ancestry checks. Card text: 'give {"commit": "<full 40-hex sha>"}; ref names such as HEAD are refused'. Test: HEAD, a branch name and a short sha each get validation, and a full sha is accepted. Optionally apply the same rule to the {"commit"}-only completion at verbs.py:917.

output.summary: F1 resolved: record_stale (record-only staleness) now drives the routine downgrade and previous.output, so reclaimed new/reopened runs keep their capability; verified against card.py:79/191, verbs.claim and frontier.py:219. New material finding F2: checkpoint overrides accept any string, which done_record resolves with rev_parse in the main repository; {"commit":"HEAD"} usually resolves to an ancestor of the work branch, passes the ancestry check, and records the wrong checkpoint silently. The design's claim that literal HEAD is refused is false at read_dev. Require a full 40-hex sha for overrides.

spec:
Dogfooding Release 1 (2026-11-01) found several places where workers were misled or under-informed by cards and lease verbs. Fix them together:
1. `abandon` prints the exact restart command (`start G X --as <LABEL> --reclaim`). Plain `start` after an abandon is refused without `--reclaim`, which misled the root agent.
2. A card issued by a reclaim (or any start) whose node's inputs changed since the previous attempt carries `stale_because` and a pointer to what changed (for example the old and new spec blobs or a diff command). Today it says `reason: reclaim` only.
3. A `submit` refused because findings arrived while the worker ran (responses are checked against findings live at submit time) lists those findings with their text and targets, so the worker can answer them without re-reading state.
4. The card's `output_schema` states that a finding reopens its target node. Coordinate with G1000, which adds materiality and non-blocking notes; this item only makes the consequence explicit in whatever form G1000 lands.
5. The task card's top-level `renew` prose and `commands.renew` are merged or clearly labelled, so the runnable command is obvious.
6. CLI_USAGE documents that ZZZOPS_TRACE records network git and gh calls only.
Acceptance: engine tests for 1-3 (abandon output; reclaim card after a spec edit has stale_because; submit refusal lists the new findings); card snapshot tests for 4-5; docs for 6. No extra fetches. Coordinate with G1014, which adds live-lease entries and renew's inputs_changed (reuse its helper for item 2).
title: Make task cards and lease verbs explain restarts, staleness and findings
